claims.text: Increasing the spark plasma sintering temperature improves the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermet.
Increasing the spark plasma sintering temperature produces a denser microstructure.
Increasing the spark plasma sintering temperature reduces porosity in the consolidated cermet.
Increasing the spark plasma sintering temperature improves interfacial bonding between the boride and metallic phases.
Higher sintering temperature accelerates diffusion during consolidation.
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced porosity minimize pathways for molten-aluminum penetration.
Minimizing molten-aluminum penetration pathways reduces corrosion of the cermet.
Samples processed at the higher sintering temperature will have lower corrosion penetration depths than samples processed at the baseline temperature.
Samples processed at the higher sintering temperature will exhibit less degradation in molten aluminum than baseline samples.
The expected improvement is limited to a suitable sintering-temperature window.
Excessively high sintering temperatures may induce undesirable phase transformations.
Excessively high sintering temperatures may cause grain coarsening.
Phase transformations or grain coarsening caused by excessive sintering temperature may negate or reverse the corrosion-resistance improvement.
